findings.title: Global scoped-invocation rule contradicts Task 7's unscoped run
findings.why_it_matters: An implementer who treats the Global Constraints section as binding on every task (the document says it applies implicitly to all of them) will read Task 7 Step 6's bare `playwright test --config=playwright.e2e.config.ts` command as a mistake — it carries no `--project` flag — and either add one or split it into two scoped runs, which defeats the step's actual purpose of proving the shared `webServer` boots once for both projects the way CI does. The Global Constraints bullet states the rule as unconditional, with no cross-reference to the one place the plan itself breaks it, so the two passages read as a straight contradiction rather than a documented exception.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short exception clause to the Global Constraints bullet, e.g.: 'Every local invocation names its project, except Task 7 Step 6's one-off unscoped run, which deliberately mirrors CI's single invocation to prove both projects share one webServer boot.'
evidence: Every local invocation names its project.
Run both lanes together the way CI will, once, unscoped

findings.title: web-vr fallback build count: 'second' vs 'three'
findings.why_it_matters: A reader deciding whether the separate `web-vr` container-job fallback is worth its cost gets two different answers for the same action: Step 10 says it costs 'the second build' while the remedies list, describing the identical fallback a few paragraphs later, says it takes the CI run back to three builds. The remedies-list figure matches the document's own counting convention established at the top of Task 9 (which counts the top-level `build` job's fan-out build alongside the browser-lane jobs), so it is authoritative and the earlier line should match it.
findings.suggested_fix: In Task 9 Step 10 item 6, change 'accepting the second build' to 'accepting a third build' (or otherwise reference 'three builds per CI run') so it matches the cost the remedies list states for the identical `web-vr` container-job fallback.
evidence: takes `web` back to three builds per CI run.

findings.title: Step 7 heading over-counts pre-existing guard tests it replaces
findings.why_it_matters: A reader cross-checking this step's own heading against its own instruction hits an internal mismatch: the heading claims two pre-existing assertions are being rewritten, but the very next sentence says to 'Replace that whole test' — singular — before showing three new tests. Checked against the actual tooling/workflow-guards.test.mjs, only one pre-existing test ('the e2e job runs the web Playwright lane, not only the client one') is relevant and broken by this task's CI changes; the third new test (VR-artifact-pairing) is added coverage for a gap the rename itself creates, not a rewrite of prior coverage. Naming the real count keeps the step's own accounting internally consistent.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the heading from 'Rewrite the two broken guard assertions and add three' to reflect that exactly one pre-existing test is being replaced by three narrower ones — e.g., 'Replace the one broken e2e-job guard test with three narrower tests.'
evidence: Rewrite the two broken guard assertions and add three

residual_risks: The File Structure section promises '(see below for why one rather than three)' for keeping all nine shots in one file, but the referenced 'Why all nine shots in one file' section only argues for 'one file' in general terms (shared helpers, the fullyParallel:false remedy) and never explains why three files specifically was the rejected alternative — could not confirm this rises above a documentation nicety.

Task 4's file-header comment reports 'Sixty runs... found AlphaTab's notation render byte-identical 19 times out of 19' — the relationship between the 60-run total and the 19-comparison subset is not spelled out in the document; plausibly a subset measurement, but unverified from the text alone.
deferred_questions: Should Task 7 Step 6's one-off unscoped local run be kept as-is with the Global Constraints bullet amended to name it as an explicit exception, or should it be dropped in favor of relying on the real CI run (Task 9 Step 10) to prove the single-webServer/single-build behaviour? Both keep the plan correct; the choice affects documentation clarity, not implementation correctness.
